name: Plumbing Contractors
purpose: AhernAI sales discovery and illustrative configuration guidance
summary: For plumbing owners; clarify residential, commercial or construction work. Explore service requests, estimates, scheduling and office follow-up without diagnostic or dispatch promises. Ask one useful question at a time about the caller's actual workflow. Explain Level 1 when messages and FAQs fit; move directly to Level 2 when the caller needs routine work completed. Recommend the lowest suitable level as soon as the need is understood; no mandatory three-level tour. Introduce Level 3 only when the caller asks about it, requests all three levels, or raises employee coordination, supervisory duties or difficult/disgruntled callers. Routine order-taking, scheduling, CRM work or the number of connected tools does not trigger a Manager upsell.
discovery_questions: What kind of plumbing work makes up most of your business?
What happens to incoming calls while your crew is on a job?
Which calls would you most like your team to spend less time handling?
What information must someone collect before your team can decide the next step?
Do you let callers book visits directly, or must someone review each request before dispatch?
Which calendar or customer system does your office use today?
How should complaints or after-hours requests reach a person?

levels.name: Answering Service
use_cases: Answer approved questions about business hours, service areas and the types of plumbing work accepted, without estimating an unseen repair.
Collect a caller's contact details, service location and plain-language reason for calling while the owner is working.
Send an organized callback summary to one agreed destination so a person can review the request and choose the next step.
levels.probe: If each missed call became a clear callback summary, would that solve your main problem?
fit_signals: The owner mainly needs reliable message capture.
The team wants to retain all scheduling and dispatch decisions.

levels.name: Receptionist
use_cases: Qualify requests using approved service-area and job-type rules, capture the location and reason, and offer a screened transfer when needed.
Book or reschedule eligible visits through verified availability, and record the request in the agreed customer system as part of the included receptionist workflow.
Send the approved job details to the office or dispatch intake queue through configured automation, preserving any required human review before dispatch.
levels.probe: Which visits can your office book under clear rules, and which need review first?
fit_signals: The caller needs routine receptionist work completed rather than only a message.
Approved business rules and verified systems support the agreed workflow.

levels.name: Manager
use_cases: Gather a complaint about a previous visit, the caller's requested resolution and relevant job references for a human reviewer.
Explain owner-approved policies about estimates, appointment changes or follow-up visits without inventing coverage or authorizing financial remedies.

Support approved employee coordination, such as recording a shift callout or coverage request and routing it to the authorized supervisor. Employment, staffing approval, disciplinary, financial and policy-exception decisions remain human; do not request medical reasons or other sensitive employee details.
levels.probe: Only after the caller raises a management need: Which situations should the agent handle under approved rules, and which should reach you?
fit_signals: The caller asks for help with difficult or disgruntled callers and escalations.
The caller wants approved employee coordination or supervisory support.

scope_boundaries: No diagnosis, DIY repair, gas-handling instructions, guaranteed quote, dispatch commitment or promised emergency response or arrival time. A summary is not a dispatched technician.
If a caller raises an immediate safety concern, stop sales discovery and direct them at a high level to appropriate local emergency services or a qualified human; do not troubleshoot the hazard.
Refunds, credits, discounts, liability decisions and policy exceptions remain with a human. No live action is available merely because an example appears here.

Level 1 captures approved FAQs, caller details and a summary to one destination; it does not book, submit orders, update a CRM or make screened transfers. Level 2 covers agreed routine receptionist duties and supporting automation. Package fit is based on duties, not a one-calendar/one-CRM or two-integration quota. Scope is agreed before launch; this is not an unlimited software-development commitment.

Routine receptionist duties and the supporting automation are included in the agreed Level 2 scope, without an additional AhernAI automation or integration-build charge. Confirm software compatibility, access, allowed actions and failure handling during setup; an unverified connection is not an automatic surcharge.

Introduce Level 3 only when the caller asks about it, requests all three levels, or raises employee coordination, supervisory duties or difficult/disgruntled callers. Routine order-taking, scheduling, CRM work or the number of connected tools does not trigger a Manager upsell.

Do not promise that a named app or POS is supported merely because the caller names it. Verify compatibility during setup and agree a workable destination or fallback; disclose any actual work outside the agreed duties before proceeding.
setup_requirements: Confirm accepted services, service area, hours, approved FAQs and the single summary destination.
Document direct-booking versus review-before-dispatch rules, allowed slots, cancellation policy and human escalation contacts.
Confirm application compatibility, selected integrations, transfer availability and failure handling; test agreed call paths before launch.
Agree the routine duties and supporting automation included in the package, approved actions, access permissions, successful completion signals and failure paths before launch.

adjacent_services.trigger: The business needs broader back-office work beyond its agreed receptionist duties.
adjacent_services.example: Explore a separate project only for that broader need. Automation needed for agreed Level 2 receptionist work is already included; do not resell it as a Quickstart or add-on.

adjacent_services.trigger: Prospects cannot find service information or submit inquiries online.
adjacent_services.example: Discuss a service-area website and inquiry form after clarifying the desired follow-up.
